# Reproducible post-deploy corpus selection (multi-pattern `--glob`) — Already delivered

Discovered during LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW (discovered-from:LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW).

## Status: Already delivered

All 4 acceptance criteria were implemented and shipped in commit
`ddb45c3c` as part of **LP-0MUYFBVHX004Z0UE** ("Extend prompt_cache_analysis.py
with throughput + client-visible first-byte latency").

Evidence, per AC:

1. **Post-deploy corpus selection, recorded in `meta`.** `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py`
   accepts `--cache-ram-filter MIB`, which keeps only files whose cache-state
   lines declare that `--cache-ram` cap — llama-server logs carry no
   timestamps, so the cap is the reproducible selector. The JSON artifact
   records `meta.glob` (verbatim), `meta.globs` (split), `meta.cache_ram_filter_mib`
   and `meta.files` (the selected llama-server files). `harness._iter_llama_files`
   already spans both rotation schemes (`llama-server.log`, `llama-server.1.log`,
   `llama-server.log-YYYY-MM-DD.gz`), so no hand-built symlink corpus is needed.
2. **Backward compatible.** `_split_patterns` returns a one-element list for a
   single `--glob`, so single-pattern behaviour is unchanged (verified by the
   existing single-glob test path in `test_multi_pattern_glob`).
3. **Unit tests covering the new selection.** `test_multi_pattern_glob`
   (multi-file comma-separated corpus + single pattern) and
   `test_cache_ram_filter_selects_matching_files` (23552 MiB filter isolates
   the post-deploy file).
4. **Existing prompt-cache tests pass.** `python3 -m pytest tests/test_prompt_cache_analysis.py`
   → **18 passed**.

Usage is documented in `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md`
(`--cache-ram-filter 32768` post-deploy corpus, lines ~179–203).

## Disposition

**Close as delivered.** The scope of this item was absorbed into
LP-0MUYFBVHX004Z0UE (commit `ddb45c3c`, status completed). No further
implementation work remains; the item is a duplicate of that scope and is
closed without advancing to planning.

## Related work

- LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW — Verify prompt-cache right-sizing on a live post-deploy window (discovered-from; done)
- LP-0MUYFBVHX004Z0UE — Extend prompt_cache_analysis.py with throughput + first-byte latency (impl source; completed)
- LP-0MUPPAC7R0053J8L — Right-size the llama-server prompt cache (parent effort; completed)
- LP-0MUYFC3C5004TCYN / LP-0MV5HSZ51005CM7A / LP-0MV5HSUHF002MDPG — cache-ram raise / verify items
- `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` — documents the filter-based post-deploy corpus

## Constraints

None — this is a retrospective disposition of already-shipped work.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

  "(A) Record the AC-verified-as-delivered status, mark as delivered/duplicate

  `test_multi_pattern_glob` (line 254) and `test_cache_ram_filter_selects_matching_files`
  (line 274) in `tests/test_prompt_cache_analysis.py`; 18 tests pass;
  `git log -S` shows the work landed at `ddb45c3c` under LP-0MUYFBVHX004Z0UE.

data.description:
## Goal

Characterise and, if needed, bound the residual risk introduced by the
in-flight prefill-liveness signal (LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC, commit 9b7c505c).

## Context

`_extend_lease_during_prefill` now refreshes `last_progress_ts` whenever the
upstream request is still in flight with no error (`prefill_in_flight=True`).
This removes the dependency on `/slots` (unobservable under load) and was
verified live: long local prefills now complete instead of being killed at the
180s no-progress timeout.

Residual risk: "connection open, no transport error" is not the same as "the
backend is actively prefilling". A request that llama-server accepts but never
progresses now holds a dispatch lease until `local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`
(900s) rather than being released at 180s. Two such holds were observed via the
900s ceiling during the cheap-mode verification (`dispatch_first_byte_timeout
ceiling=900s`).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A hermetic test reproduces the "accepted but never progressed" shape (open
   in-flight request, no first byte, no `/slots` state) and asserts the lease is
   held only until `local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`, then released and the
   upstream cancelled.
2. Evidence is recorded on whether the 900s hold can starve the local pool
   (e.g. N held leases with no local progress while other sessions are denied
   local), and the impact quantified.
3. If the impact is material, propose a bound tighter than 900s for the
   no-first-byte case (or another discriminating signal), with the trade-off
   against killing genuinely long prefills stated.
4. Full project test suite passes if code changes are made.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MS0ZLMO0002E69O** – Fix _should_skip_local to use dynamic new-token threshold instead of binary ratio check (completed)
- **LP-0MUXQNPKE008K9MP** – Verify liveness-based prefill lease extension on a live post-deploy window (completed)
- **LP-0MSQF3RRQ0070LGP** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog/worktrees/wl-LP-0MSMF5LXO006YDNM-allow-in-flight-sessions-to-keep-using-t/proxy/config.yaml:93 — Unexpected indentation (invalid-syntax) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 180s, accepted, actively, another, asserts (+87 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: acceptance, accepted, accepts, another, asserts (+84 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: acceptance, accepted, accepts, another, asserts (+84 more)

## Key files

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_extend_lease_during_prefill()` (in-flight prefill liveness), `_get_prefill_in_flight_count()`, and the dispatch-lease ceilings (`local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`, `local_dispatch_first_byte_timeout_seconds`)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — local dispatch admission gate that consumes the prefill-in-flight count
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_lease_extension.py` — existing hermetic coverage for the lease extension; extend it for the accepted-but-never-progressed shape
- `proxy/config.yaml` — documented defaults/comments for the dispatch-lease and first-byte ceilings
